title: KMS/HSM Fallback Playbook and Console Operator Flows
content:
TL;DR: Working playbook and operator-facing console flows for KMS/HSM integration + graceful fallbacks when customer KMS is slow/unavailable or HSM is temporarily inaccessible. Focus is admin console UX (choices, warnings, recovery actions) and an operator semaphore model for key migration/rotation operations. NOT final; this is an operational draft for discussion with SRE and security.

Goals
- Make the admin console give clear, actionable choices when a private deployment can't reach customer KMS/HSM.
- Surface exact impact of each fallback (security posture, audit trail, SLA impact) in concise microcopy.
- Define operator semaphore/workflow to prevent concurrent key operations that could brick instances.
- Include CLI/drag-drop import UX for emergency key rotation and a documented recovery path for on-prem HSM outages.

High-level UX principles
- Avoid cryptic errors: use plain-language status ("KMS unresponsive — using local proxy" vs "502").
- Default to safest behavior: when in doubt, prefer read-only / in-flight-request-only fallbacks; require explicit confirmation for automatic downgrade.
- Expose the blast radius: show which clusters, model endpoints, and audit streams will be affected by a change.
- Provide a one-click "safety rollback" from any manual fallback action that runs an automated verification checklist.

Operator semaphore model (concept)
- Single per-deployment semaphore that gates: key-rotation, key-import, key-decommission, KMS-proxy enable/disable.
- Visual state in console: Locked (who, why, timestamp) / Pending / Free
- Actions that acquire the semaphore must show a recommended hold time and estimated completion (e.g., rotate key across 12 nodes = ~7m)
- If a user tries to acquire a held semaphore, present: owner, reason, ETA, and option to request takeover (creates a ticket + audit log entry).
- Semaphore timeouts: default 1h for manual ops; operators can extend with justification; automatic rollback if no heartbeat.

Fallback options to present in console (priority order + microcopy)
1) Retry with backoff (recommended) — "Temporary network issue; we'll keep trying for 5 minutes. No change to cryptography settings."
2) Use hosted KMS-proxy (soft-fallback) — "Encrypts with Redwood-managed keys stored in a temporary, encrypted cache. This reduces cryptographic isolation; audit log will show proxy usage. Use for brief outages only."
3) Use cached-wrapped-keys (for read-only traffic) — "Serves inference using previously unwrapped keys where safe; no new keys will be provisioned."
4) Manual key import (operator) — "Upload a wrapped key file via CLI or secure console. Requires HSM validation step."
5) Pause endpoints (fail-safe) — "Stops new requests to selected endpoints until KMS is reachable. Good for high-security customers."

For each option show: security impact (low/medium/high), expected downtime, audit trace location, revert button.

Wireframe notes (console screens to add/modify)
- Deployment > Security > Key management panel
  - Top banner: current KMS status (green/yellow/red) with short reason and "details" link
  - Semaphore status: small pill with owner initials + tooltip with details
  - Quick actions: Retry / Use proxy / Import key / Pause endpoints
  - Action confirmation modal: show blast radius and require typing the deployment name for destructive choices
- Per-endpoint dropdown: toggle to opt-in for proxy fallback for this endpoint (persisted policy)
- Timeline view: shows recent KMS operations, who triggered them, and verification results (checksums, wrap/unwrap success)

CLI/Import UX
- CLI: redwood private kms import --file wrapped-key.bin --fingerprint 0xabc123 --reason "emergency-rotation"
  - CLI validates fingerprint and uploads to a signed staging bucket. Console shows pending validation and expected verification ETA.
- Console import flow for non-CLI users: drag-and-drop only for wrapped keys with a required policy file; upload restricted to admin role with 2FA.
- Always require HSM attestation token when importing wrapped material (or mark flow as "software-only" with visible warning).

Edge cases & failure modes (we need concrete test plans)
- Customer KMS replication lag across regions => console should allow per-region KMS mapping and show divergence window.
- HSM unreachable but KMS reachable => allow key operations that don't require HSM, disallow unwraps needing HSM. Provide clear message.
- Stale cached-wrapped-keys used for inference -> metric: percent requests served from cache; show in timeline.
- Partial rotate success (only subset of nodes) => automation to roll back to previous key after X failed nodes; show remediation steps in console.
- Key rollback requires re-sealing older keys in HSM; include a "Rollback checklist" button.

Audit & compliance notes
- All fallback actions MUST append a human-readable justification; this becomes part of the audit event.
- Exportable compliance report: timeframe, actions, operator ids, KMS key fingerprints, HSM attestation tokens (hashed), and endpoints affected.
- Retention: keep fallback events for 7 years for enterprise regs; allow admin to request S3 export.

Backlog grooming (tickets rough)
- PD-1204 console: add semaphore UI and API (priority: P0, estimate: 5d)
- PD-1205 add "Use hosted KMS-proxy" flow and billing flag (P1, 4d)
- PD-1206 CLI: wrapped key import + fingerprint validation (P1, 3d)
- PD-1207 per-endpoint fallback policy (P2, 2d)
- PD-1208 audit export endpoint + report generator (P1, 3d)
- PD-1209 automated rollback on partial-rotate failure (P0, 6d)
- PD-1210 acceptance test matrix and chaos tests for KMS/HSM outages (P0, 4d)

Open questions / decisions
- Can we allow a default tenant-level "proxy allowed" policy with per-endpoint overrides? Security wants explicit opt-in by default — product prefers opt-out. Need security signoff (ask: Priya).
- How long can we safely store Redwood-managed unwrapped keys in cache during proxy mode? (SRE + security discussion; propose 24h limit, rotating cache AES keys every 2h.)
- Do we add an API to expose semaphore state to external automation (yes/no)? Benefits: automations can avoid conflicting operations. Risk: external actors could hold semaphore indefinitely.
- Mechanic for takeover: should takeover require 2 approvals for highly-sensitive deployments? (suggestion: two-click escalation tied to SSO groups.)

TODOs (immediate)
- [ ] Get sec review on proxy storage TTL and HSM attestation requirements (Priya)
- [ ] Draft microcopy for 4 modals: Retry, Proxy, Import key, Pause endpoints (Maya)
- [ ] Proto semaphore UI in Figma and link to this doc (Luca)
- [ ] Create PD-1204..PD-1210 in Jira and schedule grooming with eng/SRE
- [ ] Prepare acceptance test cases for PD-1210 (SRE)

Notes to reviewers
- This is intentionally operator-centric (assumes admin console user is an ops/infra engineer). For the "self-serve" onboarding experience we should later produce a simplified path that hides advanced fallbacks behind an "advanced" toggle.
- Please focus review on the semantics of each fallback and the audit/rollback guarantees. UX polish will come after the flow is agreed.

Quick links (working)
- KMS integration spec: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/PD/KMS+HSM+integration+overview
- HSM attestation RFC: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/PD/HSM+attestation+RFC
- Jira backlog board: https://jira.redwood.ai/browse/PD
